trace.definition: To copy a line or shape by drawing over it.

tracing.definition: copying a drawing by following its lines onto another surface

tragic.definition: very sad and serious, often involving death or disaster

transfer.definition: to move an image, ink, or design from one surface to another

transform.definition: to change something from one form or appearance into another

trend.definition: a general direction of change or development over time

trim.definition: to cut the edges of something neatly

tube watercolour.definition: watercolour paint that comes in a tube

turpentine.definition: A strong-smelling liquid used for thinning some paints and cleaning certain art tools.

ujamaa.definition: a Makonde sculpture style showing people connected together, symbolising unity and support

undefined.definition: not clear in shape, meaning, or limits

unity.definition: the quality of all parts working together as one whole

utilitarian.definition: made to be useful or practical.

UV light.definition: a type of light used in printing to harden emulsion

value.definition: the lightness or darkness of a colour or tone.

value scale.definition: a range of tones from light to dark used to show value.

variety.definition: the use of different kinds of parts to make an artwork more interesting

vellum.definition: a smooth paper-like material that can be partly see-through and is used for designs

venue.definition: a place where an event, activity, or gathering happens

versatile.definition: able to be used in many different ways

vibrant.definition: very bright and full of strong colour

viewer.definition: a person who looks at an artwork

viewfinder.definition: a tool used to help an artist choose and frame the part of a scene to draw

viscosity.definition: how thick or sticky a liquid is

viscous.definition: thick and sticky, not flowing easily

visibility.definition: how easily something can be seen

visual arts.definition: art forms that people mainly enjoy by looking at them.

visual texture.definition: a texture that looks real to the eye but may not actually be felt by touch.

visualise.definition: to form a picture in your mind of how something will look

visuals.definition: pictures, images, or things that can be seen and used to show ideas

warm colours.definition: colours like red, yellow, and orange that give a feeling of warmth

wash.definition: a smooth, even layer of thin paint spread over a surface

washout booth.definition: a place or sink area where a screen is washed after exposure

waste.definition: Using more of something than needed, or materials that are thrown away.

waste management.definition: the process of collecting, handling, and disposing of waste safely

water soluble.definition: able to dissolve or mix in water

water-based.definition: made with water as the main liquid

watercolour.definition: a type of paint mixed with water

watercolour painting.definition: painting made by using water-based colours on a surface

watercolour paper.definition: special paper made for painting with water-based colours because it can soak up water without being damaged easily

waterfall.definition: a place where water falls from a high place to a lower place

wax.definition: a soft substance that can be melted or shaped.

wet-on-dry.definition: a painting technique where wet paint is put on dry paper

wet-on-wet.definition: a painting technique where wet paint is put on wet paper

wholeness.definition: the state of being complete and fully joined together

wildlife.definition: animals living in nature, not kept by people

woodcut.definition: A type of relief printing made by carving a design into wood.

workspace.definition: the area where someone does their work

zigzag.definition: a line or shape with sharp turns first one way and then the other

zinc.definition: a metal that can be used to make printing plates
